headline: Explicit models of unobserved processes recover gene-level rates and hidden zeros
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: Simulation-based and likelihood-based methods now infer gene-level rates and sampling zeros directly rather than absorbing them as noise.
synthesis: The dominant thread is replacing a simplifying assumption with an explicit model of an unobserved process. Neural posterior estimation infers gene-specific recombination and mutation rates in bacterial genomes via simulation, and TestNet-PA models sampling zeros in presence-absence data through an EM-based quasi-likelihood aimed at FDR control in co-occurrence networks. The SARS-CoV-2 lineage study estimates growth rates from graph-Laplacian spectral features with machine learning, a less generative route. The viral embedding benchmark evaluates genomic language models against k-mer and MinHash baselines and is adjacent rather than central. What is new is the target: local, gene-level rates and zero-inflation are inferred directly rather than absorbed into noise.
